motion: Has science refuted religion, or does that claim overreach by confusing scientific method with scientism and by ignoring non-scientific forms of evidence?

burdens.description: Show that science supports a unified naturalistic account and leaves no evidenced supernatural causal role needed to explain the world.
burdens.successCriteria: Identify a central supernatural claim that would make an observable difference, then show the predicted difference is absent or that a tested natural account explains the same observations without it.

burdens.description: Show that religious belief or its claimed epistemic authority is better explained by natural, cultural, or psychological processes than by religious truth.
burdens.successCriteria: Tie at least one representative religious truth claim to observable cultural, psychological, or historical patterns and show those patterns favor a natural origin or failed religious prediction over special access to truth.

burdens.description: Show that the inference from successful natural science to the refutation of religion illicitly excludes relevant non-scientific evidence or exceeds science's proper scope.
burdens.successCriteria: Identify a central religious claim and a relevant historical, testimonial, philosophical, or personal evidential route that the pro case does not test, or expose a necessary anti-religious premise not established by scientific findings.

burdens.description: Show that substantive religious claims remain logically compatible with established science and that scientific description need not exhaust explanation.
burdens.successCriteria: Name a substantive religious doctrine and the scientific result alleged to conflict with it, then give a coherent interpretation or distinct explanatory level that preserves the doctrine without denying the result.

source.limitations: English auto-generated captions contain ASR errors and have no speaker diarization. Attribution uses the announced debate order and clear uninterrupted turn boundaries. No local audio was supplied, so only high-confidence turns were selected and rapid or interleaved exchanges were excluded.

inventoryProtocol.selectionStatement: Selected the first two load-bearing constructive acts per side from the opening cases. Divided the post-opening exchange from the moderator's transition into rebuttals through the final substantive closing into four equal chronological quarters and selected the earliest two qualifying load-bearing responsive acts in each quarter, carrying no quota because each quarter filled two. Candidates failing high-confidence attribution, atomicity, excerpt length, or load-bearing relevance were skipped and logged.

moves.selectionRationale: This is the next distinct load-bearing pro act: it grounds science's comparative epistemic reliability in methods designed to counter human bias and wishful pattern detection.

moves.speaker: Ian Hutchinson
moves.sourceExcerpt: Richard Dawkins says the existence of God is a scientific hypothesis like any other, I think he holds forth the foremost fallacy of the 21st century anti-theist arguments. Well, I think it's because they subscribe to the philosophical doctrine of scientism. The erroneous belief that all the real knowledge there is is science.
moves.selectionRationale: This is the earliest load-bearing con act: it distinguishes a question about God's existence from a scientific hypothesis and identifies the contrary scope assumption as scientism.

moves.speaker: Ian Hutchinson

moves.selectionRationale: This is the second distinct load-bearing con act: it argues that scientism neither follows from science nor validates itself, so the pro side cannot treat it as a scientifically established bridge from science to religious refutation.
